title.zh: 卷五十八 志第二十七: 儀衞志四
title.raw: 卷五十八 志第二十七: 儀衞志四 Volume 58 Treatises 28: Ceremonial Guards 4

sentences.zh: 儀衛誌四

translations.literal: Ceremonial Guards Treatise, Part Four
translations.idiomatic: Ceremonial Guards, Part Four

sentences.zh: （儀仗）〉

translations.literal: (Ceremonial Paraphernalia)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Ceremonial Paraphernalia)〉

sentences.zh: 帝王處則重門擊柝，出則以師兵為營衛，勞人動眾，豈得已哉。

translations.literal: When emperors remain in residence, heavy gates are barred and the night-watch clappers are struck; when they go forth, they take the army as camp guard—it taxes the people and moves the multitudes; can this truly be avoided?
translations.idiomatic: When emperors stay in the palace, heavy gates are barred and the night-watch is beaten; when they travel abroad, armies must serve as their camp guard. Such measures burden the people and mobilize great crowds—yet can any ruler truly do without them?

sentences.zh: 天下大患生於大欲，不得不遠慮深防耳。

translations.literal: The great calamities of the realm spring from great desires; one cannot but take far-seeing thought and deep precautions.
translations.idiomatic: The greatest perils facing the realm spring from unchecked ambition; a ruler has no choice but to plan far ahead and guard against every threat.

sentences.zh: 智英勇傑、魁臣雄藩於是乎在，寓武備於文物之中，此儀仗所由設也。

translations.literal: Valiant heroes, wise and brave, eminent ministers and mighty frontier lords are thereby present; martial readiness is lodged within ritual regalia—this is why ceremonial paraphernalia is established.
translations.idiomatic: It is here that the brave, the wise, and the valiant stand together with eminent ministers and powerful frontier lords, with martial readiness concealed within ceremonial regalia. This is why ceremonial guard paraphernalia was instituted.

sentences.zh: 金吾、黃麾六軍之仗，遼受之晉，晉受之後唐，後唐受之梁、唐，其來也有自。

translations.literal: The paraphernalia of the Jinwu, Yellow Banner, and Six Armies—Liao received them from Jin, Jin from Later Tang, Later Tang from Liang and Tang; their origin has its source.
translations.idiomatic: The regalia of the Jinwu Guards, the Yellow Banner, and the Six Armies: the Liao inherited it from the Jin, the Jin from Later Tang, and Later Tang from Liang and Tang—each transmission had its own lineage.

sentences.zh: 耶律儼、陳大任舊《志》有未備者，兼考之《遼朝雜禮》雲。

translations.literal: Where Yelü Yi's and Chen Daren's earlier Records were incomplete, both were also examined against the Miscellaneous Rites of the Liao Dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: Where the earlier monographs by Yelü Yi and Chen Daren were incomplete, the Miscellaneous Rites of the Liao Dynasty was consulted as well.

sentences.zh: ○國仗

translations.literal: ○ National Paraphernalia
translations.idiomatic: ○ National Paraphernalia

sentences.zh: 王通氏言，舜歲遍四嶽，民不告勞，營衛省、征求寡耳。

translations.literal: Master Wang Tong said: Shun each year visited all four sacred peaks, yet the people did not complain of fatigue—camp guards were few and requisitions light.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tong observed that even when Emperor Shun toured the four sacred peaks every year, the people did not complain of exhaustion, because his camp guards were few and his levies light.

sentences.zh: 遼太祖匹馬一麾，斥地萬里，經營四方，未嘗寧居，所至樂從，用此道也。

translations.literal: Liao's Taizu, with a single horse and one command, extended territory ten thousand li, managed the four quarters, never dwelt at ease; wherever he went people gladly followed—he employed this same principle.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizu of Liao, with a single horse and one command, extended his domain ten thousand li and toured the four quarters without ever settling in one place; wherever he went, people gladly followed—he employed this same principle.

sentences.zh: 太宗兼制中國，秦皇、漢武之儀文日至，後嗣因之。

translations.literal: Taizong also ruled China; the ceremonial protocol of the First Emperor of Qin and Emperor Wu of Han arrived day by day, and later heirs followed it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong also ruled China, and each day brought more of the ceremonial protocol of the First Emperor of Qin and Emperor Wu of Han; his successors followed suit.

sentences.zh: 旄頭豹尾，馳驅五京之間，終歲勤動，轍跡相尋。

translations.literal: With yak-tail banners and leopard-tail insignia, they raced among the Five Capitals; the whole year was labor and movement, wagon ruts following one upon another.
translations.idiomatic: With yak-tail banners and leopard-tail insignia, they raced among the Five Capitals, laboring throughout the year so that wagon ruts followed one upon another.

sentences.zh: 民勞財匱，此之故歟！

translations.literal: The people grew weary and coffers empty—is this not the cause!
translations.idiomatic: The people grew weary and the treasury ran dry—was this not the cause?

sentences.zh: 遼自大賀氏摩會受唐鼓纛之賜，是為國仗。

translations.literal: Liao, from the time the Mohe clan of the Greater He received Tang's gift of drums and banners, took this as national paraphernalia.
translations.idiomatic: From the time the Mohe clan of the Greater He received Tang's gift of drums and banners, this became the Liao national regalia.

sentences.zh: 其制甚簡，太宗伐唐、晉以前，所用皆是物也。

translations.literal: Its regulations were quite simple; before Taizong's campaigns against Tang and Jin, everything used was of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: Its regulations were quite simple; before Emperor Taizong's campaigns against Tang and Jin, everything used was of this sort.

sentences.zh: 著於篇首以見艱難創業之主，豈必厚衛其身雲。

translations.literal: It is placed at the head of the chapter to show a founder who toiled through hardship to build the realm—not one who necessarily sought lavish personal protection.
translations.idiomatic: It is placed at the head of the chapter to show a founder who toiled through hardship to build the realm—not one who necessarily sought lavish personal protection.

sentences.zh: 十二神纛十二旗十二鼓曲柄華蓋

translations.literal: Twelve spirit banners, twelve flags, twelve drums, curved-handle parasols
translations.idiomatic: Twelve spirit banners, twelve flags, twelve drums, and curved-handle parasols

sentences.zh: 直柄華蓋

translations.literal: Straight-handle parasols
translations.idiomatic: Straight-handle parasols

sentences.zh: 渤海仗

translations.literal: Bohai paraphernalia
translations.idiomatic: Bohai Regalia

sentences.zh: 天顯四年，太宗幸遼陽府，人皇王備乘輿羽衛以迎。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianxian, Taizong visited Liaoyang Prefecture; the Human Emperor King prepared the imperial carriage and feathered guard to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of the Tianxian era (929), Emperor Taizong visited Liaoyang Prefecture, and the Human Emperor King prepared the imperial carriage and feathered guard to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 乾亨五年，聖宗東巡，東京留守具儀衛迎車駕。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Qianheng, Emperor Shengzong toured east; the Eastern Capital regent prepared ceremonial guards to welcome the imperial procession.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of the Qianheng era (983), Emperor Shengzong toured the east, and the regent at the Eastern Capital prepared the ceremonial guard to welcome the imperial procession.

sentences.zh: 此故渤海儀衛也。

translations.literal: This was the former Bohai ceremonial guard.
translations.idiomatic: This was the ceremonial guard inherited from Bohai.

sentences.zh: 漢仗

translations.literal: Han paraphernalia
translations.idiomatic: Han Regalia

sentences.zh: 大賀失活入朝於唐，娑固兄弟繼之，尚主封王，飫觀上國。

translations.literal: Da He Shihuo entered court at Tang; the Suogu brothers succeeded him, married imperial princesses and were enfeoffed as kings, and feasted their eyes on the superior realm.
translations.idiomatic: Da He Shihuo attended court at Tang; the Suogu brothers succeeded him, married imperial princesses and were enfeoffed as kings, and feasted their eyes on the splendors of the Tang court.

sentences.zh: 開元東封，邵固扈從，又覽太平之盛。

translations.literal: At the Kaiyuan eastern feng sacrifice, Shaogu followed in attendance and again beheld the grandeur of the Great Peace era.
translations.idiomatic: At the Kaiyuan eastern feng sacrifice, Shaogu followed in attendance and again beheld the grandeur of the High Tang.

sentences.zh: 自是朝貢歲至於唐。

translations.literal: From then on tribute missions came yearly to Tang.
translations.idiomatic: From then on, tribute missions arrived at Tang every year.

sentences.zh: 遼始祖涅裏立遙輦氏，世為國相，目見耳聞，歆企帝王之容輝有年矣。

translations.literal: Liao's founding ancestor Nieli established the Yaonian clan, generation after generation serving as chief minister of state; by eye and ear he had long admired and yearned for the emperor's splendor.
translations.idiomatic: The founding ancestor of Liao, Nieli, established the Yaonian clan and served for generations as chief minister of state; through what he saw and heard, he had long admired and yearned for the splendor of the Tang emperors.

sentences.zh: 遙輦致鼓纛於太祖帳前，曾何足以副其雄心霸氣之所睥睨哉！

translations.literal: When Yaonian presented drums and banners before Taizu's tent, how could that ever suffice for the lofty gaze of his ambitious, hegemonic spirit!
translations.idiomatic: When the Yaonian clan presented drums and banners before Taizu's tent, how could such gifts ever satisfy the soaring ambitions his hegemonic spirit had long fixed upon!

sentences.zh: 厥後交梁聘唐，不憚勞珝。

translations.literal: Thereafter they exchanged embassies with Liang and sent missions to Tang, not fearing the toil of the road.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter they exchanged embassies with Liang and sent missions to Tang, undaunted by the hardships of the journey.

sentences.zh: 至於太宗，立晉以要冊禮，入汴而收法物，然後累世之所願欲者，一舉而得之。

translations.literal: As for Taizong, he installed Jin to demand investiture rites, entered Bian and collected ritual objects—then what generations had desired was obtained in one stroke.
translations.idiomatic: When it came to Emperor Taizong, he installed Later Jin to demand investiture rites, entered Bianjing and seized the ritual regalia—and thus what generations had long desired was obtained at last in a single stroke.

sentences.zh: 太原擅命，力非不敵，席卷法物，先致中京，槊棄山河，不少顧慮，誌可知矣。

translations.literal: Taiyuan acted on its own authority; its strength was not unequal, yet it swept up ritual objects and sent them first to Zhongjing, casting aside mountains and rivers with a spear and scarcely a second thought—its intent may be known.
translations.idiomatic: When Taiyuan acted on its own authority, its strength was hardly inferior—yet it swept up the ritual regalia and sent them first to Zhongjing, casting aside mountains and rivers with scarcely a second thought. Its priorities are plain enough.

sentences.zh: 於是秦、漢以來帝王文物盡入於遼；

translations.literal: Thus the ritual regalia of emperors since Qin and Han all entered Liao;
translations.idiomatic: Thus the ritual regalia of emperors since Qin and Han all passed into Liao hands;

sentences.zh: 周、宋按圖更制，乃非故物。

translations.literal: Zhou and Song remade them according to diagrams—they were no longer the original objects.
translations.idiomatic: while Zhou and Song remade their own according to diagrams—they were no longer the original objects.

sentences.zh: 遼之所重，此其大端，故特著焉。

translations.literal: What Liao valued—this was the great point; therefore it is specially recorded.
translations.idiomatic: This was the great matter that Liao prized above all, and therefore it is given special record here.

sentences.zh: 三年，上在薊州觀《導駕儀衛圖》，遂備法駕幸燕，禦元和殿，行入閣禮。

translations.literal: In the third year, the emperor at Jizhou viewed the Diagram of Escort Ceremonial Guards, then prepared the full imperial equipage to visit Yan, ascended the Yuanhe Hall, and performed the entering-the-pavilion rite.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, the emperor viewed the Diagram of Escort Ceremonial Guards at Jizhou, then prepared the full imperial equipage to visit Yan, ascended the Yuanhe Hall, and performed the entering-the-pavilion rite.

sentences.zh: 六年，備法駕幸燕，迎導禦元和殿。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, he prepared the full imperial equipage to visit Yan; escort led him to the Yuanhe Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, he again prepared the full imperial equipage to visit Yan and was escorted to the Yuanhe Hall.

sentences.zh: 大同元年正月朔，備法駕至汴，上御崇元殿，受文武百僚朝賀。

translations.literal: On the first day of the first month of the first year of Datong, with full imperial equipage he reached Bian; the emperor ascended the Chongyuan Hall and received the civil and military hundred officials in court congratulation.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the first month of the first year of Datong (947), with full imperial equipage he reached Bianjing; the emperor ascended the Chongyuan Hall and received the civil and military officials in court congratulation.

sentences.zh: 自是日以為常。

translations.literal: From then on this became daily routine.
translations.idiomatic: From then on this became the daily routine.

sentences.zh: 二月朔，上御崇元殿，備禮受朝賀。

translations.literal: On the first day of the second month, the emperor ascended the Chongyuan Hall, prepared the rites, and received court congratulation.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the second month, the emperor ascended the Chongyuan Hall, performed the full rites, and received court congratulation.

sentences.zh: 三月，將幸中京鎮陽，詔收鹵簿法物，委所司押領先往。

translations.literal: In the third month, about to visit Zhongjing Zhenyang, an edict ordered collection of outer guard ritual objects, entrusted to the responsible offices to escort and send ahead.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, as he prepared to visit Zhongjing at Zhenyang, an edict ordered the collection of outer-guard ritual regalia and directed the responsible offices to escort them ahead.

sentences.zh: 未幾鎮陽入漢，鹵簿法物隨世宗歸於上京。

translations.literal: Before long Zhenyang fell to Han; outer guard ritual objects followed Emperor Shizong back to the Upper Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Zhenyang fell to the Han, and the outer-guard ritual regalia followed Emperor Shizong back to the Upper Capital.

sentences.zh: 四月，皇太弟李胡遣使問軍事，上報曰，朝會起居如禮。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, the Imperial Younger Brother Li Hu sent envoys to inquire about military affairs; the emperor reported that court assemblies and daily conduct proceeded according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month, the Imperial Younger Brother Li Hu sent envoys to inquire about military affairs; the emperor reported that court assemblies and daily conduct proceeded according to ritual.

sentences.zh: 是月，太宗崩，世宗即位，鹵簿法物備而不禦。

translations.literal: That month Taizong died; Shizong succeeded to the throne—the outer guard ritual objects were prepared but not employed.
translations.idiomatic: That month Emperor Taizong died and Emperor Shizong succeeded to the throne; the outer-guard ritual regalia were prepared but not employed.

sentences.zh: 穆宗應歷元年，詔朝會依嗣聖皇帝故事，用漢禮。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yingli under Emperor Muzong, an edict ordered court assemblies to follow the precedent of the Succession Sage Emperor, using Han rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Yingli era (951), Emperor Muzong issued an edict directing that court assemblies follow the precedent of the Succession Sage Emperor and employ Han rites.

sentences.zh: 四年，燕京留守具儀衛導駕入京，上御元和殿，百僚朝賀。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, the Yanjing regent prepared ceremonial guards to escort the imperial procession into the capital; the emperor ascended the Yuanhe Hall and the hundred officials offered court congratulation.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, the regent at Yanjing prepared the ceremonial guard to escort the imperial procession into the capital; the emperor ascended the Yuanhe Hall, and the officials offered court congratulation.

sentences.zh: 是後，儀衛常事，史不復書。

translations.literal: Thereafter, routine matters of ceremonial guard were no longer recorded in the histories.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, routine matters of ceremonial guard were no longer recorded in the histories.

sentences.zh: 人之數凡四千二百三十有九，馬之數凡千五百二十。

translations.literal: The total of persons was 4,239; the total of horses was 1,520.
translations.idiomatic: The total number of personnel was 4,239; the total number of horses was 1,520.

sentences.zh: 得諸本朝太常卿徐世隆家藏《遼朝雜禮》者如是。

translations.literal: Obtained from the household collection of Xu Shilong, Director of Rites of our dynasty, of the Miscellaneous Rites of the Liao Dynasty—it is thus.
translations.idiomatic: This is as recorded in the Miscellaneous Rites of the Liao Dynasty, preserved in the household collection of Xu Shilong, Director of Rites of our dynasty.

sentences.zh: 至於儀註之詳，不敢傅會雲。

translations.literal: As for the details of ceremonial regulations, I dare not force a conflation.
translations.idiomatic: As for the finer points of ceremonial protocol, I dare not force a conflation where the sources do not agree.
